retailer_risk_assessment.primary_exposure_pillars: Green Claims Integrity; Supply-Chain Human Rights
retailer_risk_assessment.key_evidence: Member-owned governance; ETI Base Code sourcing standard; 100% Fairtrade across core own-brand lines (tea/coffee/sugar/bananas/cocoa) since 2017; no notable ESG enforcement history found

First UK retailer with externally validated net-zero targets; disclosed 40% Scope 1-2 cut vs 2020/21 baseline (2025); Polytag UV-tag packaging traceability on milk; specific dated packaging/circularity targets (70% circular design by 2030)

10/10 on 2026 RSPO Shared Responsibility Scorecard; ~99% segregated RSPO palm oil; historical 'first carbon neutral major retailer' framing is the kind of broad claim EU Green Claims Directive/EmpCo specifically targets even when backed by real programs
retailer_risk_assessment.source: corporate.marksandspencer.com Palm Oil Policy Aug 2026; sustainablefoodbusiness.com

retailer_risk_assessment.key_evidence: Detailed, specific, tracked own-brand plastic reduction (29% since 2017, targeting 40% by 2026) and food-waste reduction (43% since 2016); private multinational large enough to eventually fall under CSRD-equivalent group reporting thresholds, not yet matched by UK-specific standardized disclosure

4,500 tonnes of packaging removed (2024 report); flexible-plastic traceability via Greenback's eco2Veritas; same private-multinational CSRD-readiness gap as Lidl; ingredient-level EUDR sourcing traceability at company level not yet publicly evidenced

Directly sells/packages goods online (JV with M&S); proactively investing in EPR-compliance tooling (Polytag UV tags, live on milk range + 100+ own-label SKUs); one of very few pure online-only grocers, so it is effectively a first-mover test case for how pEPR enforcement gets applied to online-only retail — genuine regulatory-ambiguity exposure even with strong compliance intent

ASA has an active enforcement history in this exact space: Sainsbury's has previously been rebuked by the ASA for misleading Fairtrade tea claims, and was one of two parties (with Tesco) in a set of 'contrasting' ASA rulings on plant-based environmental claims — real, adjudicated precedent, not just accusation
retailer_risk_assessment.source: thedrum.com; lexology.com ASA contrasting rulings; asa.org.uk

retailer_risk_assessment.jurisdiction_footprint: UK; Ireland; Czech Republic; Slovakia; Hungary
retailer_risk_assessment.primary_exposure_pillars: Green Claims Integrity; Climate & Emissions Disclosure
retailer_risk_assessment.key_evidence: UK's largest grocer with the widest multi-country regulatory surface of the UK-focused set; publicly accused (media, not yet a formal finding in the sources found) of greenwashing over 'biodegradable' teabag claims; also a party to the same ASA plant-based-claims dispute as Sainsbury's

retailer_risk_assessment.primary_exposure_pillars: Climate & Emissions Disclosure; Green Claims Integrity
retailer_risk_assessment.key_evidence: Real, specific curbside-recyclable packaging rollout (replaces ~735k lbs plastic film/yr) and Climate Pledge (net-zero by 2040); but sits inside a much larger group with an existing, separate pattern of labor/antitrust regulatory scrutiny that colors investor and regulator perception of grocery-specific claims

retailer_risk_assessment.primary_exposure_pillars: Climate & Emissions Disclosure; Supply-Chain Human Rights
retailer_risk_assessment.key_evidence: Owned 67.5% TDR Capital / 22.5% Mohsin Issa / 10% Walmart since 2024; leveraged buyout structure with less mandatory public-disclosure cadence than listed peers (Tesco/Sainsbury's/M&S); no LSE-driven ESG reporting obligation

CD&R-owned since 2021 (delisted after 54 years on LSE); £6.6bn acquisition debt; sold fuel forecourts (up to £2.5bn) and 7 warehouses (sale-leaseback) post-acquisition, drawing explicit political criticism over asset stripping; CD&R has a public net-zero-British-farms-by-2030 pledge with a hard, checkable deadline and not yet independently verified progress

Made a high-profile, absolute 2018 pledge to ban palm oil from own-label products (the Greenpeace 'Rang-tan' campaign) — the pledge was later partially reversed; a reversed absolute environmental pledge is precisely the pattern the EU Green Claims Directive/EmpCo and equivalent UK rules are designed to catch

retailer_risk_assessment.entity: Getir (quick-commerce archetype — currently inactive in UK)
retailer_risk_assessment.key_evidence: Exited UK, Germany, Netherlands and the US on 29 Apr 2024 (~1,500 UK jobs affected) after unit-economics collapse — not itself an ESG enforcement action, but the dark-store/gig-rider quick-commerce model structurally combines higher packaging-per-basket than consolidated grocery baskets with rider-classification exposure; included as the model archetype since a re-entrant would carry the same structural risk

Already has a real, settled enforcement outcome: $46.5M settlement (announced Oct 2022) with the San Diego City Attorney over worker misclassification, covering ~308,000 workers; operates in a post-AB5 landscape (upheld by 9th Circuit, Jun 2024) where the marketplace/contractor model itself is the exposed structural assumption, not a peripheral practice
retailer_risk_assessment.source: grocerydive.com; bamlawca.com; lexology.com IC misclassification update
